concepts.def: Discrete: countable outcomes (binomial, Poisson). Continuous: any value in an interval (normal, exponential).
PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]². Spread of distribution. SD = √Var(X).
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Statistical Distributions — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Statistical Distributions brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Statistical Distributions.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between area and perimeter?
options: Perimeter is the total distance around the outside; area is the amount of surface inside (measured in square units).
£24.50, by multiplying £3.50 by 7.
Area and perimeter are different names for the same measurement.
Area is half the perimeter for any shape.

mcqs.q: If 5 pens cost £3.50, how much do 7 pens cost?
options: Take the average of the probabilities on the branches.
£4.90 — find the unit cost (£0.70 per pen), then multiply by 7.
£24.50, by multiplying £3.50 by 7.
£5.50, by adding £2 to £3.50 because there are 2 more pens.

mcqs.q: On a probability tree, how do you find the probability of a sequence of outcomes along one path?
options: £24.50, by multiplying £3.50 by 7.
Take the average of the probabilities on the branches.
Multiply the probabilities along that path.
Add the probabilities along the path.
